outcome: Give farm operations director / food quality head a governed method to improve litres water per kg crop yield using soil moisture, crop stage and local evapotranspiration, with final decisions…
overview: Precision Irrigation Water Scheduling addresses operational records arrive through different systems, supervisors reconstruct evidence manually, and decisions are difficult to audit in agriculture and food production operations. The first proof of value uses soil moisture, crop stage and local evapotranspiration. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is litres water per kg crop yield, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.
kpi: litres water per kg crop yield

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: soil moisture, crop stage and local evapotranspiration; define litres water per kg crop yield and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Farm Operations Director / Food Quality Head.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including line-by-line reconciliations against known business transactions.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
